resource.name: aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device
resource.description: Provides an IAM Virtual MFA Device. All attributes will be stored in the raw state as plain-text. Read more about sensitive data in state. A virtual MFA device cannot be directly associated with an IAM User from Terraform. To associate the virtual MFA device with a user and enable it, use the code returned in either base_32_string_seed or qr_code_png to generate TOTP authentication codes. The authentication codes can then be used with the AWS CLI command aws iam enable-mfa-device or the AWS API call EnableMFADevice.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource enables the creation and management of virtual MFA devices for enhancing IAM user security in AWS. It is commonly used to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for IAM users by generating TOTP authentication codes via a base-32 seed or QR code. While Terraform cannot directly associate the virtual MFA device with a user, this resource facilitates the setup process, allowing users to integrate MFA devices with IAM users using AWS CLI or API commands for improved account protection and compliance.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic setup of an AWS IAM Virtual MFA Device using the `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource, showcasing how to define a virtual MFA device with the `virtual_mfa_device_name` argument. Users can learn how to create and configure a named virtual MFA device for enhancing IAM user security.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the virtual MFA device, typically representing its ARN or resource ID. While optional, setting this argument can help users reference or manage the MFA device in other Terraform configurations or workflows, ensuring consistent identification and integration within IAM policies or authentication setups.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: – (Optional) The path for the virtual MFA device.
arguments.llm_summary: The `path` argument for the `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource allows users to define the hierarchical path under which the virtual MFA device is created within AWS IAM. This configuration helps organize and scope the device within a specific namespace or structure, supporting use cases like grouping MFA devices by environment, team, or application for better resource management and access control.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of resource tags for the virtual mfa device. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata or organizational labels to the virtual MFA device. This facilitates resource categorization, tracking, and management, enabling alignment with tagging strategies for cost allocation, environment identification, or compliance purposes. Tags specified here can override provider-level default tags if matching keys are present.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically merged from both provider-level default tags and resource-specific tags. This enables consistent tagging across cloud resources for purposes such as cost allocation, organization, and resource management, aligning with common practices for governance and operational visibility.

arguments.name: virtual_mfa_device_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the virtual MFA device. Use with path to uniquely identify a virtual MFA device.
arguments.llm_summary: The `virtual_mfa_device_name` argument specifies the unique name of the virtual MFA device within AWS IAM, allowing users to define and identify the device in combination with its path. Setting this argument ensures the proper association and management of the MFA device for secure multi-factor authentication workflows.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) specifying the virtual mfa device.

attributes.name: base_32_string_seed
attributes.description: The base32 seed defined as specified in RFC3548. The `base_32_string_seed` is base64-encoded.

attributes.name: enable_date
attributes.description: The date and time when the virtual MFA device was enabled.

attributes.name: qr_code_png
attributes.description: A QR code PNG image that encodes `otpauth://totp/$virtualMFADeviceName@$AccountName?secret=$Base32String` where `$virtualMFADeviceName` is one of the create call arguments. AccountName is the user name if set (otherwise, the account ID), and Base32String is the seed in base32 format.

attributes.name: user_name
attributes.description: The associated IAM User name if the virtual MFA device is enabled.
